name: scroll-fade
tagline: Lists fade, shrink and blur at whichever edge hides more content.
summary: A scrolling list wrapper that masks its own top and bottom edges and gently scales and blurs rows as they approach the hidden edge, so cut-off content tapers away instead of being sharply clipped.
appearance: A rounded bordered card with a small header row showing 'Changelog' and a release count, above a tall scroll area. Inside, one line per release: a monospaced version, a title, and a date or small pill. Rows near a scrolled edge fade and shrink.
behaviour: On scroll the wrapper measures how near it is to each end and fades that edge with a gradient mask; rows inside the fade zone also shrink slightly and blur. An edge with nothing hidden stays fully opaque, and values settle with a short animation.
demo_content: Changelog card listing 16 releases like '2.4.0 Scroll fade', each with a version, title and date or New tag.
search_phrases: fade out list edges when scrolling
blur items near cut off edge
changelog list with fading top and bottom
scrollable panel that dims hidden rows
clean cut off content edge treatment
use_when: A fixed-height list or panel scrolls but hard edges make the cut-off rows look abrupt and unfinished.
avoid_when: It edits child inline styles for scale and blur, so virtualized lists or already-transformed children can conflict.
customise: Orientation, fade size, shrink amount, blur strength, transition and an enabled flag are props; the gradient maths and edge colours are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Observes scroll, resize and DOM mutations and repaints item scale and blur on each frame.

a11y.note: Reduced-motion is honoured, but the scroll box is not focusable, so keyboard users must reach a child before arrowing through it.

polish_why: The demo card looks tidy in the code, but with no image the finish cannot really be judged.
